transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, I just keep blowing up at people. Over nothing, really. I'm an operations manager, and lately I've been snapping at my team on calls, which is bad enough, but I'm doing it to my family, too. It's just not me. I've never handled things this way, and I don't know why I can't seem to control my temper right now.
Have there been times recently when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt rested?

No, not at all. I mean, if I don't get much sleep, I definitely feel it the next day. I haven't had any times where I just ran on a couple of hours and felt completely fine or rested. Honestly, I'm usually just exhausted.
Have you used alcohol or any recreational or nonprescribed drugs recently?
No, I haven't. I don't use any kind of drugs, and I haven't really been drinking either. So, no, nothing like that.
Has there been a specific stressful event or major change in your life recently that you connect with these outbursts?
Yeah. This has been going on for about three weeks now. We had a... well, there was a valve failure at the facility, and someone got injured. Ever since that happened, I've just been like this.
Before the valve failure, had you ever had similar episodes of suddenly losing your temper?

No, not at all. I mean, sure, work gets stressful and I'd get frustrated sometimes, like anyone else, but I never just lost my temper like this. I was always pretty level-headed. This is all completely new since that day.
Since the valve failure, have you had unwanted memories of the incident that keep coming back to you?

Yeah, I do. I can just be... sitting at the kitchen table, or trying to answer some emails from home, and suddenly I'm right back there. I see the flash from that valve and the smoke in the aisle. It's like it just shoves everything else out of my head.
Since the valve failure, have you been avoiding people, places, activities, or conversations that remind you of what happened?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't been avoiding anything specifically. I still go to work, I still talk to the same people. I just... I don't go out of my way to avoid things, it's just the memories keep coming back on their own, no matter what I'm doing.
Since the valve failure, have you felt detached from yourself or as though the world around you wasn’t real?

No, I haven't really felt anything like that. I mean, I feel like myself, and everything around me feels real enough. It's just... I'm just dealing with the memories and the anger, but I don't feel disconnected from reality or anything.
Since the valve failure, have you felt unusually on guard or watchful for danger, even when you were in a safe place?

Yeah, I have. It's pretty constant, actually. Any time I hear a forklift beep or a compressor kick on... or even just the smoke alarm chirping at home, my whole body just tightens up. I immediately start looking around for exits and trying to figure out what could go wrong next. It doesn't really matter if I'm at the plant or just sitting in my own living room, I'm just always bracing for the next thing to happen.
Since the valve failure, have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, I really have. Most nights I just lie there in the dark, and it's like I can still hear that alarm going off in my head. And then when I finally do manage to doze off, I just wake up sweating. I keep having these dreams about the smoke, and... and hearing people yelling. So by the time morning rolls around, I feel like I haven't slept a wink.
Since the valve failure, have you engaged in any serious aggressive, reckless, or rule-breaking behavior beyond verbally losing your temper?

No, nothing like that. I mean, I've definitely been short-tempered and angry... but I haven't done anything reckless. I'm not getting into physical fights or, you know, breaking the law or doing anything stupid. I just get mad, but I keep it to words.
